subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser routes intentionally return the stale acted-on target ID, requiring callers to re-select, whenever a backend cannot prove post-operation continuity rather than preserving heuristic continuation?
rationale: Both choices are externally observable: accepting this patch prevents wrong-tab actions but changes recovery for clients that previously received a guessed replacement target.

options.title: Accept fail-safe stale-target recovery
options.body: Merge the backend-owned outcome design and document that callers must refresh tab selection when the original target is closed or continuity is unavailable.

options.title: Require a supported continuity owner first
options.body: Pause this PR until the relevant backend exposes a stable replacement identity for the affected route rather than returning a stale target.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-safe stale-target recovery
recommendation.body: Merge the backend-owned outcome design and document that callers must refresh tab selection when the original target is closed or continuity is unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report and current PR discussion identify this as the browser identity/recovery contract decision.
